sections.title: Iran War and the Strait of Hormuz
sections.summary: Trump vows to 'finish the job'; Araghchi dares him to 'try your luck'; Lavrov arrives in Tehran

paragraphs.heading: War of words
paragraphs.body: Trump said Washington would soon 'finish the job' against Iran unless Tehran changed course. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi replied on X that Iran emerged stronger from the last round and asked 'want to try your luck again?', adding 'we have unfinished jobs too', The Hill and JNS reported. Araghchi accused Netanyahu of pushing Washington toward another war. [[TAG:warning:escalating rhetoric]]

paragraphs.heading: Lavrov in Tehran
paragraphs.body: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov is in Tehran on Monday to meet Araghchi and President Masoud Pezeshkian. Lavrov said the talks aim at 'preventing the return of a large-scale war' and called for a return to the Pakistan-brokered framework that collapsed in July, CBS News and Kurdistan24 reported. Iran's foreign ministry framed the trip as consultations on bilateral agreements, according to Anadolu. [[TAG:info:mediation push]]

paragraphs.heading: Hormuz still choked
paragraphs.body: The UK navy counted 10 attacks on commercial ships in and near the strait last week, making October the worst month since the war's early days, CBS News reported. Araghchi said Iran's offer of a seven-day ceasefire and phased reopening, conditional on the US lifting its blockade and sanctions, still stands. Trump and CENTCOM say the route is open to all but Iranian ships, while trackers such as straits.live record traffic far below the prewar norm of about 85 transits a day. [[TAG:danger:disputed traffic]]

sections.title: Gulf, Yemen, Israel and Lebanon
sections.summary: GCC condemns Houthi strikes as drones hit Najran; Lebanon heads to US-hosted talks

paragraphs.heading: Houthi attacks continue
paragraphs.body: Saudi air defenses shot down drones near Riyadh and in the Eastern Province early Sunday, and a Houthi projectile injured six people in a residential area of Najran, Al Jazeera reported. Houthi media said a Saudi airstrike in Yemen killed at least nine people; that claim could not be verified. [[TAG:danger:Najran hit]]

paragraphs.heading: Gulf response
paragraphs.body: Gulf Cooperation Council ministers condemned the attacks and called for tighter enforcement of the arms embargo on the Houthis, Al Jazeera reported. Egypt has pledged help to Saudi Arabia, and Arab News reported coalition forces destroying incoming missiles and drones. In Yemen, government troops reported gains in Taiz as the Houthis fired missiles toward Marib.

paragraphs.heading: Gaza and Lebanon
paragraphs.body: Israeli strikes killed at least two Palestinians in Gaza on Sunday, and the IDF said weekend strikes killed a Hamas commander, according to reports compiled by Kayhan and the Times of Israel. The World Food Programme said it will end monthly aid to 500,000 Gazans because of a funding shortfall. Lebanon's military is set to attend US-hosted talks in Tampa on October 20, while Israeli forces hold a zone up to 10 km into southern Lebanon. Israel votes on October 27.

sections.title: Ukraine and Russia
sections.summary: Kyiv launches 1,000-plus drones at Russia; Trump says Zelensky never wanted to end the war

paragraphs.heading: Mass drone strike
paragraphs.body: Russia's defense ministry said it shot down 1,015 Ukrainian drones overnight into Sunday, as Ukraine hit a key oil terminal near St. Petersburg in one of its biggest drone attacks of the year, CNN and Al Jazeera reported. At least one person was killed and five injured in Russia. The strike defied Trump's demand that Kyiv stop hitting Russian energy sites. [[TAG:warning:defying Washington]]

paragraphs.heading: Trump turns on Zelensky
paragraphs.body: In a Truth Social post, Trump said he is negotiating peace and does not want to push Russia away from the table, and said Zelensky 'doesn't want to end this war, and probably never did', CBS News and CNN reported. The clash follows Friday's waiver of congressionally mandated Russia sanctions.

paragraphs.heading: 'Historic mistake'
paragraphs.body: Zelensky told NBC's Meet the Press that a US decision to side with Russia would be 'a historic mistake and a big tragedy' and that Ukraine would not prevail in that case, The Hill and the Philadelphia Inquirer reported. He said Kyiv still wants to trust Trump and linked restrictions on Starlink-based service for Ukrainian drones to a 'message from the American government', which the administration denies. Kremlin officials welcomed the rift. [[TAG:danger:alliance strain]]

sections.title: Markets and the Economy
sections.summary: China beats at 4.5%; oil slips to ~$108 on Russia waiver; US futures bounce before big earnings

paragraphs.heading: China beats
paragraphs.body: China's economy grew 4.5% year on year in the third quarter, ahead of the 4.4% consensus and up from 4.3% in the second quarter, Xinhua and FXStreet reported. Growth for the first nine months was 4.6%, within Beijing's 4.5%–5% target. Analysts credited strong exports while consumer spending and property stayed weak. [[TAG:success:above forecast]]

paragraphs.heading: Oil eases
paragraphs.body: Brent fell about 2% to around $107.60–$108 a barrel in Asian trading Monday after Friday's settlement near $109.86, its highest since May, as traders priced in more Russian fuel reaching markets after Trump's sanctions waiver, ADVFN and FinanceFeeds reported. Analysts said Hormuz disruption and attacks on Saudi energy sites still support prices. Reports differ slightly on the exact level. [[TAG:info:Brent ~$108]]

paragraphs.heading: Futures and Asia
paragraphs.body: US stock futures rose ahead of a week with more than 70 S&P 500 earnings reports, including Tesla, Meta and Netflix, Bloomberg via Yahoo Finance reported; Nasdaq 100 futures gains ranged from 0.7% to 1.4% depending on the source. In Asia, one market preview had the Nikkei down 1.2% and Taiwan down 1.4% early Monday, while another reported a 2% Nikkei drop at the open.

sections.title: US Politics
sections.summary: Trump approval at record-low 33%; Texas early voting opens with Senate race a dead heat

paragraphs.heading: Record-low approval
paragraphs.body: The Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos poll, conducted October 9–13, put Trump's approval at 33% and disapproval at 66%, a record low for the series, with 52% strongly disapproving. Democrats lead the generic ballot 52% to 44% among likely voters, and only 21% approve of his handling of the cost of living. Axios reported NBC and Fox polls at 34% and 36%. [[TAG:danger:33% approval]]

paragraphs.heading: Texas votes
paragraphs.body: Early voting in Texas opens Monday and runs through October 30. A CBS News/YouGov poll has Democrat James Talarico at 51% and Republican Ken Paxton at 49% among likely voters, a statistical tie, and a University of Houston survey also shows Talarico up two points, CBS Texas and Houston Public Media reported. Both candidates held dueling rallies Sunday. [[TAG:info:early voting opens]]

paragraphs.heading: Other fights
paragraphs.body: Trump said renovation of a historic Washington golf course will start in November despite a judge's order requiring prior court notice, US News reported. Speaker Mike Johnson said Republicans will hold the House.

sections.title: Europe
sections.summary: Lecornu vows France won't be intimidated; Pope Leo returns to the Angelus window

paragraphs.heading: France after the riots
paragraphs.body: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said France would not be 'intimidated' by violence after Saturday's cost-of-living protests and pointed to a Senate bill that would make rioters financially liable for damage, Anadolu reported. Turnout was about 550,000 by the interior ministry's count and 800,000 by organizers' count, France 24 reported; arrest figures range from about 400 to 1,200 depending on the source and time of day. [[TAG:warning:figures disputed]]

paragraphs.heading: Roots of the unrest
paragraphs.body: The movement began with high school protests in late September over under-resourced schools and has since drawn in unions and 'yellow vest' groups, PBS reported. The government accuses the far left of stoking it; organizers say it is spontaneous.

paragraphs.heading: Pope Leo's return
paragraphs.body: Pope Leo XIV led the Angelus from the Apostolic Palace window on Sunday before about 15,000 people, his first major public appearance since lung cancer surgery, Al Jazeera and CNN reported. He said the delicate phase was behind him and he would gradually resume his duties; Cardinal Pietro Parolin said his schedule may be adjusted. His surgeon sees no clinical obstacle to the November 6–17 Latin America trip. [[TAG:success:recovering]]

sections.title: Global Roundup
sections.summary: Kenya confirms eighth Ebola case; Congo outbreak reaches an eighth province

paragraphs.heading: Ebola in Kenya
paragraphs.body: Kenya confirmed its eighth Ebola case, a 49-year-old man quarantined after likely exposure to the country's first patient, just over two weeks after that first case, ABC Australia and Al Jazeera reported. Up to 128 contacts, including health workers, remained in quarantine as of Sunday, and Kenya has tightened border screening. [[TAG:danger:8 Kenya cases]]

paragraphs.heading: Congo's outbreak
paragraphs.body: Congo's Bundibugyo-strain outbreak has spread to an eighth province and has killed at least 4,000 people since May, NBC News reported, calling it the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record. The WHO's Africa director said cases are falling in some pockets even as the outbreak spreads geographically. Uganda has declared itself free of the disease.
